analysis.title: The AI dollar is here
key_insights: Over the prior 24 hours, AI-related stocks and the dollar sold off at the same time. DB has argued that the dollar's risk-off properties cannot be taken for granted in an AI-driven equity correction.
Foreign equity inflows into the US currently finance the entire US current account deficit, while equity market concentration is very high. DB calls this reliance historically unprecedented.

DB estimates roughly 90% of the $20+ trillion of US equities owned by foreigners reflects price appreciation rather than underlying buying. For every $1 of US equities bought there are roughly $10 of equities that could be sold.

For ten years the US stock/dollar correlation has been negative, which encouraged foreign investors to hold US equity exposure unhedged. When an equity shock is US-centric, the correlation flips positive, so the USD adds to equity losses and pushes investors to hedge. DB compares this to the price action around Liberation Day.

Confirmation of a 'USD down, equity down' dynamic should show up in lower US real yields. DB says the main driver of the combined move of higher rates and higher equities this year has been a large rise in capex expectations, so lower real yields plus lower equities would point to those expectations being cut.
DB takes no view on the outlook for the AI ecosystem. Its point is that risks to the dollar are more two-sided than the market has priced over the last few weeks.
risk_factors: An AI-driven US equity correction could cause the dollar to fall along with stocks instead of rising as a haven.
Foreign investors may hedge their US equity exposure if the stock/dollar correlation turns positive, which would add selling pressure on the USD.
Capex expectations for AI could be downgraded, which would lower both US real yields and equities.

tension_points.bull_case: For ten years US stocks and the dollar have been negatively correlated, so the dollar has hedged equity losses and foreign investors have held US equities unhedged.
tension_points.bear_case: When the shock is US-centric the stock/dollar correlation turns positive, so the USD adds to equity losses and foreign holders have reason to hedge.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A fall in US real yields alongside lower equities would confirm the 'USD down, equity down' dynamic. The view is weakened if real yields do not fall with equities.
